html:
A kind of invisible radiation that passes through soft flesh but not bone, discovered by the German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen at the University of Würzburg on 8 November 1895.

Röntgen was experimenting with a cathode ray tube wrapped in black card when he saw a screen across the room begin to glow. Some unknown ray was passing through the card. He called it X, for unknown. Within weeks he had made an image of the bones of his wife's hand, with her ring, and sent out his paper. The news spread around the world in days.

Doctors used X-rays at once to find broken bones and bullets, and soon in war surgery. The discovery also led Henri Becquerel to find radioactivity in 1896, and Marie Curie to study it, opening up atomic physics. Röntgen won the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 and refused to patent his discovery. Early workers did not know the rays were dangerous, and many suffered burns and cancer before safety rules came in.
sum: A kind of invisible radiation that passes through soft flesh but not bone, discovered by the German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen at the University of Würzburg on 8 November 1895.
